findings.description: The data bucket is created as public with no blocking of public access and no ACL restricting it. This exposes all objects, including potentially sensitive data, to unauthenticated read/write over the internet.
The data bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so objects stored in it are unencrypted at rest, violating encryption of sensitive data requirements.
The financials bucket holds financial data but has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
The operations bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so its objects are stored in plaintext at rest.
The data_science bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving objects unencrypted at rest even though it is the active data processing bucket.
The customer-master object is uploaded to the unencrypted data bucket without server_side_encryption, so the sensitive file is stored in plaintext at rest.
The operations bucket does not have logging configured to the logs bucket, removing audit trail visibility into access to operations data.
The public data bucket has no access logging, eliminating the ability to audit who accessed or modified the exposed objects.
The financials bucket has no access logging, removing audit trail visibility into access to financial data.
